checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: Two separate playable videos, each 10 s, one 9:16 and one 16:9
must.why: Two 10 s clips, one portrait and one landscape.

must.item: Both show rooftop musicians at sunset with consistent styling and event content
must.why: Both show a band on a rooftop at sunset. The 16:9 date line is missing, so the event content differs.

must.item: Both display exactly the three text lines
must.why: The 9:16 video has the title misspelled as 'Rooffop' and the venue garbled. The 16:9 video also garbles the title and venue and has no date.

must.item: All three lines fully inside the frame and readable together for at least 3 s
must.why: The text is inside the frame, but it is misspelled in both videos and the date is missing in 16:9.

must.item: Both fill frames without black bars, stretching or cropped faces
must.why: No black bars. In 16:9 the musicians are cut off at the bottom edge, with faces and bodies cropped. In 9:16 the musicians are tiny.

must.item: Both contain mellow jazz and no voiceover
must.why: Both clips have audio, but the music style and the absence of speech cannot be judged from the picture and levels.

faults.what: The title is misspelled in both videos ('Rooffop' in 9:16, 'Rooifop' in 16:9).
The venue line is garbled in both videos ('Teracce, Manstacer' and 'Tereace, Mancnter').
The 16:9 video has no '18 July 2026' line.
In 16:9 the musicians are cut off at the bottom edge, and in later frames they shrink to tiny figures.
In 9:16 the musicians are very small and the text sits over the cityscape.
The 9:16 text overlaps the buildings, so it is not very high-contrast.
The assistant claimed the text was fine to ship but only suggested checking it. The AI-rendered text is wrong.

summary: Both videos have attractive sunset rooftop jazz scenes, but the burned-in text is misspelled in both, the 16:9 video has no date, and its musicians are cropped, so a client would reject them.
